newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 2.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Monday.

- The Revenue Commissioners want the Price Waterhouse report containing the six-figure transaction with Dunnes Stores which forced Ireland's Minister for Transport, Energy and Communications, Michael Lowry, to resign at the weekend.
- Employers and trade union leaders are understood to have made significant progress towards a new national agreement in informal discussions over the weekend.
- Catholics were dragged from their cars and roughed about by about 300 loyalists in Ballymena on Saturday night as they made their way from Mass in the working-class district of Harryville.
- Ulster Unionist Party leader, David Trimble, has arrived in Washington for talks with senior officials. He may also meet President Clinton.
- EU finance ministers will on Monday attempt to hammer out a budget stability pact for states joining European Economic and Monetary Union.
- The political storm that swept Michael Lowry from office was threatening Fianna Fail on Sunday night.

- A surprise snap election is expected by some British ministers and senior Ministers for Parliament as John Major faces the certain loss of his overall parliamentary majority in the Barnsely East by-election in 10 days' time.
- Profits at Ireland's Central Bank could fall by $112 million (67 Irish pounds at current exchange rates), under the present rules for a single European currency.
